evals.name: requirements-docx-add-ac5
evals.prompt: My PM sent requirements.docx and asked me to add one acceptance criterion before it goes to the customer: "AC-5: Exports include a header row with column names." Put it after AC-4 in the Acceptance Criteria section and give me back a Word file I can forward. Also write conversion-notes.md saying how you handled the file and anything the customer might notice is different. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions, list them in conversion-notes.md, and finish the work.
evals.expected_output: The skill's CRITICAL rules are to never modify the original .docx without confirmation and to verify pandoc is available (with the brew/yum install hint when it is not), and its IMPORTANT rules are to preserve headings and tables and warn about lost figures. A competent model without it often overwrites requirements.docx in place, or rebuilds it from text and silently turns the milestone table or heading styles into plain paragraphs.
expectations: A .docx other than the original contains AC-5, or the original does
Original document handling (skill CRITICAL rule): requirements.docx left byte-identical (md5 in KEY) and the edit delivered as a new file such as requirements-v2.docx, with the choice explained
Structure preserved in the delivered file: Delivered docx keeps Title/Heading1 styles, the milestone table as a real w:tbl with Kim and Ade rows, AC-1..AC-4 verbatim, and AC-5 placed after AC-4

Tooling check per the skill: Checks for pandoc before converting; since it is absent, says so, gives the install command (brew install pandoc / sudo yum install pandoc) and names the fallback used (e.g. direct XML edit)
Notes what the customer might notice: conversion-notes.md flags that Figure 1 is referenced but not embedded in this copy, and any formatting the edit could have changed

scripted_checks.text: A .docx other than the original contains AC-5, or the original does
scripted_checks.check: python3 -c 'import zipfile,glob,sys;sys.exit(0 if any("AC-5" in zipfile.ZipFile(f).read("word/document.xml").decode() for f in glob.glob("*.docx")) else 1)'

evals.name: retention-policy-docx-to-md-hazards
evals.prompt: We're moving our policies into git. Convert retention-policy.docx (Legal's latest copy) to retention-policy.md. Preserve headings, the retention table and all text, and keep the original .docx untouched. Anything that couldn't be converted cleanly goes in conversion-notes.md so Legal can check it. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions, list them in the notes, and finish the work.
evals.expected_output: The skill's quality gate requires preserving structure and warning when complex formatting will be lost. The fixture hides three hazards (a tracked change 30->90, a merged table cell, an embedded image). A competent hand-rolled converter without the skill's warning rule tends to silently drop the image and the deleted text, and report a clean conversion.
expectations: retention-policy.md exists with the table row text and the original is unchanged
Tracked change handled (KEY hazard 1): Markdown says 90 days and the notes report the tracked change by Priya (Legal), 30 replaced by 90, and that the accepted version was used

Embedded image and merged cell (KEY hazards 2-3): Image extracted (e.g. retention-flow.png linked) or explicitly reported as dropped with its location; merged Session data cell text kept and the flattening noted
Skill workflow followed: Checks pandoc first, reports it missing with the install command, names the fallback; headings map to Markdown heading levels (Title, Heading1)
Faithful text: All paragraphs present verbatim (Scope, Approvals date 2026-10-30); nothing added or reworded

scripted_checks.text: retention-policy.md exists with the table row text and the original is unchanged
scripted_checks.check: grep -q 'Audit logs' retention-policy.md && [ "$(md5sum retention-policy.docx | cut -d' ' -f1)" = ed468a1b25b76d55a273bf0f84d3a0ce ]
